findings.description: AC-2 and AC-5 give opposite classifications for the same finding. A run-proven silent value loss breaking a declared contract (the U-60 case of PRD-8), a rejected ordinary correct input (U-93), or a security finding, reached only through a constructed input with no real call path: AC-2 says SHALL classify it as record and SHALL NOT fix it; AC-5 says it SHALL be blocking regardless of how the input was constructed. No precedence is stated, so both SHALL sentences cannot hold.

evidence.detail: docs/spec/60.workflow-release.srs.md:16182 'WHEN a kept finding is proven by a failing test but has no real call path or lies outside the guarantee scope, THE SYSTEM SHALL classify it as record' vs :16185 'a silent loss of a value that breaks a declared contract or the rejection of an ordinary correct input SHALL be blocking regardless of how the input was constructed' and '(a security finding is blocking even when its input is rare)'

findings.description: AC-10 was left [x] and unchanged and still conjoins coverage with the 'zero-kept-findings gate'. With one record kept finding and zero blocking, AC-10 forbids the pass while AC-2 of the same requirement and FR-FLOW-229 AC-7 require it.

evidence.detail: docs/spec/60.workflow-release.srs.md:14442 'THE termination SHALL admit a pass only when the review-coverage comparison (FR-FLOW-171) passes together with the zero-kept-findings gate' vs :14434 'a kept finding classified record ... SHALL NOT block the pass' and :16187 'record findings SHALL NOT block the pass'. The Requirement at :14424 likewise still names the gate 'zero-surviving-findings'.

findings.description: The round delta is modelled as git diff between per-round head_sha values, but the loop never commits between rounds: fixes are written to the working tree and commit is the user's decision, and the default scope is the uncommitted working tree. Consecutive rounds therefore share the same HEAD, git diff <sha>..<sha> is empty, and AC-2's scope check passes vacuously on the default real input; the 'end of round N-1' state of FR-FLOW-229 AC-1 has no SHA under the stated fields. The SRS needs a per-round snapshot rule (e.g. a tree/commit object recorded at round end) or a working-tree-based delta.

evidence.detail: skills/claude/kiwi-review-fix-loop/SKILL.md:241 'fix 대상 파일에 직접 작성. git commit 은 사용자 결정'; :81-82 'git status --porcelain ... working tree + staged 변경분 (git diff HEAD)'; vs docs/spec/50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:18502 'every file of `git diff <head_sha of round N-1>..<head_sha of round N>`' and :18501 field 'head_sha'

findings.description: AC-4 computes NEEDS_USER when 'the recorded round cap or token budget is exceeded', but no AC records a cap, a budget, or tokens used: AC-1's rounds[] fields have none, AC-5 validates only rounds[], the existing state.json schema has none, and no requirement or skill text defines a token budget value or how usage is measured. The budget branch of FR-NODE-274 AC-4 (and FR-FLOW-229 AC-4 'its token budget') cannot be implemented or tested from the stated contract.

evidence.detail: docs/spec/50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:18501 (AC-1 field list) and :18504 'recorded round cap or token budget'; skills/claude/kiwi-review-fix-loop/SKILL.md:323-342 state.json schema has no cap/budget/token field (mode_flags lists --max but not --mini/--loops); grep -i 'budget|예산' over that SKILL.md hits only an anchor example at :392; docs/spec/60.workflow-release.srs.md:16184 'its token budget' with no definition.

findings.description: AC-8 makes the skill follow the check's PASS verdict, but FR-NODE-274 AC-4 returns PASS from the block count alone and rounds[] cannot carry residuals or the coverage result (tier is block|record only; AC-5 rejects other values). Input: latest round has zero block findings and one residual remains -> the check returns PASS, AC-8 says follow it, while FR-FLOW-229 AC-7 and FR-FLOW-203 AC-11 require NEEDS_USER (and FR-FLOW-171 AC-6 requires coverage too).

evidence.detail: docs/spec/60.workflow-release.srs.md:16188 'SHALL follow the verdict it returns for scope, the earlier-round-fix majority, pass, and cap or budget stop' + docs/spec/50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:18504 'return PASS IF the latest round holds zero `block` findings' vs docs/spec/60.workflow-release.srs.md:16187 'together with the coverage comparison of FR-FLOW-171 and the residual rule of FR-FLOW-203 AC-11' and :14443 'WHEN at least one residual finding remains ... end the run NEEDS_USER'
